37 Three resistors are connected in series with a battery, as shown. The battery has negligible
internal resistance.
120 Ω
6.0 V
180 Ω
150 Ω
What is the potential difference across the 180  resistor?
A
1.6 V
B
2.4 V
C
3.6 V
D
4.0 V

hints: Notice the $120\,\Omega$, $180\,\Omega$ and $150\,\Omega$ resistors are in series with the $6.0\text{ V}$ battery, so the same current flows through all three.
Add the three resistances to get the total resistance, then find the series current from $I = V/R$ with $V = 6.0\text{ V}$.
Use $V = IR$ for the $180\,\Omega$ resistor alone, or use the potential divider fraction $180/(120+180+150)$ times $6.0\text{ V}$.
walkthrough: In series the current $I$ is the same everywhere and the $6.0\text{ V}$ is shared in proportion to resistance. Internal resistance is negligible.
P.d. across the $180\,\Omega$ resistor is $V_{180} = I \times 180 = 0.0133 \times 180 = 2.4\text{ V}$. Equivalently $V_{180} = [180/450] \times 6.0\text{ V} = 2.4\text{ V}$.
The unit is volts and the three p.d.s $1.6\text{ V} + 2.4\text{ V} + 2.0\text{ V}$ sum to $6.0\text{ V}$, as required. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is $V = (120/450) \times 6.0\text{ V} = 1.6\text{ V}$, the p.d. across the $120\,\Omega$ resistor, not the $180\,\Omega$ resistor.

B.explanation: Series current is shared, so $V_{180} = (180/450) \times 6.0\text{ V} = 2.4\text{ V}$.

C.explanation: This is $(270/450) \times 6.0\text{ V} = 3.6\text{ V}$, the combined p.d. across the $120\,\Omega$ and $150\,\Omega$ resistors.

D.explanation: This is $(300/450) \times 6.0\text{ V} = 4.0\text{ V}$, the combined p.d. across the $120\,\Omega$ and $180\,\Omega$ resistors.
